title: Sign-in submission is anti-enumeration: identical body, status, and timing for every input
description: The POST /login handler returns the same response body, the same HTTP status, and the same wall-clock latency floor regardless of whether the submitted email is a registered principal, an unregistered address, a malformed string, or an empty value. The response never confirms or denies registration. The timing floor is set by a per-handler anti-enumeration budget that dominates the slowest legitimate branch (mint plus adapter send). Registered-branch work runs behind the same delay ceiling as unregistered-branch work.
rationale: A login endpoint that differentiates its responses on the basis of principal registration is a free enumeration oracle; an attacker with a wordlist harvests the registered set without ever guessing a password. Uniform body, uniform status, and uniform timing collapse the oracle.
